title: P95 latency regression from dynamic kernel permutation under token-length skew
creator: Omar Nguyen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-11 we observed a sustained increase in p95 token latency for several internal smoke suites and customer-facing routes after rolling runtime-1.19 which included a change to the dynamic kernel permutation logic. The regression affected mid-sized sequence lengths (128-512) with higher head counts and manifested as GPU stalls and increased memory churn, raising p95 by ~35-60% on affected fleets. This ticket captures the investigation, root cause, mitigation, and follow-ups.
timeline: 2026-03-11 03:12 UTC - Pager alert: p95 > 2x baseline for /generate on us-west-2-hosted-cluster. Ops team escalated.
2026-03-11 03:25 UTC - Canary dashboards show divergence coincident with runtime-1.19 rollout start.
2026-03-11 04:00 UTC - Rollback to runtime-1.18 for affected pools; p95 returns to baseline for rolled-back pools.
2026-03-11 06:30 UTC - Preliminary hypothesis: new dynamic kernel permutation selects permutation based on observed token-length distribution, introduced in PR #GH-7123.
2026-03-12 09:00 UTC - Reproduction in staging with synthetic workload that mimics customer token-length skew; profiler shows extra memcpy and suboptimal fused-attention kernel choice.

2026-03-13 14:00 UTC - Root cause confirmed: permutation heuristic favors kernel variant A for mid-length sequences when variance in token lengths is high, but kernel A exhibits memory access pattern regressions on GPUs with specific driver versions when head count > 32.
2026-03-14 10:00 UTC - Drafted action items and mitigation plan; creating this ticket for tracking and review.
2026-03-14 15:20 UTC - Design/PM review requested; assigned to Carmen Li for rollout plan and telemetry add-ons.
2026-03-14 17:45 UTC - Canary plan approved pending small test suite additions.
findings: Regression introduced by dynamic kernel permutation logic merged in GH-7123 as part of runtime-1.19.
Failure mode reproducible with token-length distributions that have high skew (many short prefixes + occasional long tails).
Kernel variant A (fused-attn-optimized) performs worse than fallback kernel B on GPUs with driver X.Y.Z for head_count > 32 due to additional uncoalesced writes in the tile epilogue.

Scheduler interaction: the runtime scheduler sometimes places heterogeneous sequence-length batches on the same worker and the permutation logic makes per-batch kernel choices which increase cache thrash and KV eviction frequency.
Monitoring gaps: we lacked a per-kernel selection metric and per-driver performance baseline for new permutation logic; rollback was required to restore SLAs.
No evidence of model weight corruption or correctness regressions; outputs unaffected apart from latency.

Affected customers: a small subset of customers in US-West with heavy multi-turn chat and models using >32 heads; impact classified as medium because majority of production fleets not on the problematic GPU driver version or head counts.
decisions: Immediate: rollback GH-7123 permutation changes from rollout and pin affected hosts to runtime-1.18 until mitigations land. (Done 2026-03-11).
Short-term: add canary gating to kernel permutation changes — require perf delta < 5% on p95 vs baseline across representative clusters before wide rollout.
Medium-term: implement a per-kernel telemetry histogram (by kernel variant, driver version, head count, seq_len bin) and expose in Console for ops and SRE.

Medium-term: add scheduler constraint to avoid mixing heterogeneous sequence-length batches on the same worker when permutation is enabled, or ensure permutation decisions are deterministic per-worker.
Long-term: add microbenchmarks for fused-attn kernels across driver versions and head counts to the CI perf-suite; require no-regression on p95 to merge kernel-selection heuristics.
Testing: create synthetic workload generator to stress token-length skew scenarios for pre-merge smoke tests.

acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: per-kernel selection and p95 histograms live in Console and validated against historical baseline for at least 72 hours.
Canary: new permutation changes show p95 delta <= 5% on representative clusters including driver-aware nodes during a staged rollout.
Scheduler change: no regressions introduced by the worker-level tie-breaker; smoke tests pass for heterogeneous batch scenarios.
CI: microbench baselines added and PRs modifying kernel-selection heuristics blocked until perf-suite passes.
Communication: affected customers notified and support tickets acknowledged.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy runtime-1.19 to a staging fleet containing GPUs with driver X.Y.Z and head_count >= 32.
2) Use the synthetic_sequence_skew tool (perf repo) to generate mixed traffic: 70% sequences length 32-64, 25% length 128-256, 5% length 800-1024 for 30 minutes.
3) Capture per-request kernel selection logs (enable KERNEL_SELECT_DEBUG=1) and GPU profiler traces for a 5 minute window.
4) Observe p95 latency and compare per-kernel p95 histograms; confirm kernel A chosen frequently for mid-length bins and correlates with p95 spikes.
5) Rollback to runtime-1.18 and rerun workload to confirm p95 returns to baseline.
notes: Driver versions vary across cloud providers; include driver as a first-class dimension in any perf baseline.
Consider a small fast-path heuristic: if observed seq_len variance > threshold, prefer conservative kernel to avoid edge-case memory patterns.
This incident highlights coupling between scheduler batching choices and kernel heuristics; future kernel heuristics should be scheduler-aware.
Keep rollback instructions in the runbook minimal: 'patch rollout -> pin runtime -> monitor p95 for 30 minutes'.
